influences.name: The Rolling Stones
influences.context: The music from the Stones agreed with me better because Jagger was singing more Rhythm & Blues-like and that was more my thing.

influences.name: Mick Jagger
influences.context: The music from the Stones agreed with me better because Jagger was singing more Rhythm & Blues-like and that was more my thing.

influences.name: John Lennon
influences.context: Later on Lennon also sang a bit bluesier.

influences.name: George Harrison
influences.context: Completely underrated guitar playing, fantastic guitarist actually. In Clapton's 'Badge' there's an amazing guitar break (mimics the sound) and that's Harrison, he just plays something which is immediately absolutely great!

influences.name: Little Richard
influences.context: Before we listened to Little Richard or others we liked, we didn't think about writing songs. It was a kind of revelation.

influences.name: Ringo Starr
influences.context: Every time I heard something new from Ringo I tried to play exactly like him, that's how I learned how to play the drums.

influences.name: Charlie Watts
influences.context: Of course you understand that I learned from Ringo and Charlie Watts.

influences.name: Eddie Cochran
influences.context: When we heard 'Twist and Shout' we immediately made the connection to what we liked (Little Richard, Eddie Cochran, Isley Brothers etc.).

influences.name: Isley Brothers
influences.context: When we heard 'Twist and Shout' we immediately made the connection to what we liked (Little Richard, Eddie Cochran, Isley Brothers etc.).

influences.name: Paul McCartney
influences.context: Actually Paul McCartney was a very musical bass player, like I like to play. Not just the basics but also the musical melodies.
